editorial_thesis: The practical signal today is execution-boundary design: constrain browser-capable agents, map the developer workstation’s blast radius, and make automated security remediation prove itself before a maintainer accepts it.

topic_groups.title: Sandboxed Browser Agents
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fresh August 4 integration signal earns a focused revisit of browser automation: the meaningful change is agent-browser becoming a constrained Eve extension, not another browser-agent tool list.

sources.title: Give your eve agent a browser
sources.why_selected: This is the material update to agent-browser previously tracked in July: it now has a first-party sandboxed agent integration with allowlists and model-tool controls.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: prototype a research or QA agent with an explicit client-domain allowlist. Client work: offer browser-assisted support or regression checks without giving the runtime workstation access.

sources.title: Eve + agent-browser integration guide
sources.why_selected: The useful design detail is not raw clicking; it is namespaced, inspect-then-act tools that allow policy to sit around the browser capability.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: standardize a browser extension wrapper with output caps and evidence screenshots. Client work: expose a narrow, auditable browser task instead of a general browsing agent.

sources.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sources.why_selected: Stable snapshot references support evidence-led browser interaction instead of brittle coordinate automation; the recent doctor fix also improves workstation diagnostics.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: use snapshots as review artifacts in automated web research. Client work: evaluate it where Playwright-sized stacks are unwanted.

topic_groups.title: Developer Workstation Blast Radius
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Developer workstations have been under-covered relative to cloud and package controls. Fresh primary research makes the local intersection of agents, extensions, packages, and credentials operationally specific.

sources.title: Wiz Sensor for Developer Workstations
sources.why_selected: It frames AI coding governance as endpoint-to-cloud exposure mapping rather than a standalone assistant policy.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: make a lightweight inventory of developer agents, MCP servers, package managers, and privileged tokens. Client work: use the same inventory as a discovery deliverable before deploying coding agents.

sources.title: Vercel WAF for Blob — general availability
sources.why_selected: Agent-generated media, uploads, and paid files are often treated as passive storage; edge rejection reduces both exposure and transfer cost before a request reaches the store.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: protect public artifact and upload stores with path/IP/rate rules. Client work: add storage access rules to every AI media delivery checklist.

sources.title: Share Vercel Container Registry repositories across teams
sources.why_selected: Reusable sandbox images no longer require copying artifacts or granting image-maintenance authority to every consumer team.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: publish a hardened base image to a delivery team with read-only access. Client work: separate image builders from agent-runtime consumers.

topic_groups.title: Continuous Cyber Remediation
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A security-automation coverage gap remains between scans and governed fixes. Microsoft’s late-July model/harness announcement supplies concrete evidence for evaluating a continuous find–validate–remediate loop.

sources.title: Introducing MAI-Cyber-1-Flash inside MDASH
sources.why_selected: It makes the economics of always-on security work explicit: lower-cost models handle routine work while escalation is reserved for difficult cases.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: define a staged security-agent workflow—triage, reproduce, patch proposal, test, maintainer approval. Client work: use that workflow as a scoped remediation-service blueprint.

sources.title: Defense at AI speed: Microsoft’s MDASH system
sources.why_selected: The harness is the important unit of evaluation: model selection, validation, and remediation controls need to be assessed together.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: require a proof bundle—finding, reproduction, diff, tests, and reviewer decision—for any automated security patch. Client work: make the proof bundle a contractual acceptance artifact.

sources.title: MAI-Thinking-1 technical report
sources.why_selected: Model capability assertions should be separated from deployment claims; the technical record helps frame what is known versus what the remediation harness adds.
sources.usefulness: Buildn: create a vendor evaluation note separating model evidence, harness controls, and repository-specific results. Client work: make that note part of security-AI procurement discovery.
